liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begoinais** (3 reviews): Bridge jam is hot, with the band stretching out a few extra verses; Noodling intro into Scarlet and the intense jam into Fire are singled out [15][18][22]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (2 reviews): Transition from Scarlet is sloppy, but Garcia plays strongly and the first jam runs over five minutes; Scarlet/Fire is a high-energy but meandering '83 version [15][25]
- **Spanish Jam** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the Spanish Jam nice; Spanish Jam is fleeting, followed by perfunctory playing to the end [22][25]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): First set renditions of Rooster are singled out as nice [25]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-09-13.168014.mtx.tobin.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 156 min [1]
- **gd1983-09-13.168015.dts.tobin.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 156 min [3]
- **gd1983-09-13.151515.fob.unknown.bryant.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 145 min [4]
- **gd83-09-13.aud.dodd.12483.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 152 min; rated 4.18/5 by 11 [6]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is somewhat weaker than other 1983 audience tapes, but the second set justifies downloading; Recording sits in a sweet spot with high levels [14][18]
- **gd1983-09-13.senn441.miller.83117.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 158 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [7]. Said about its sound: Open space usually cost audience tapes dynamic range, but this one is a nice exception [23]

## Around the show

- Attendee recalls a huge field outside Austin, plenty of tickets and space, bought at the gate for about $7 [16]
- Moving toward the stage between sets, the writer stepped on someone's wife; she seemed okay [16]
- Manor Downs was a good venue where the Dead typically played well [23]
- Reviewer ranks this version of the combo among the best Brent-era ones, alongside 11/1/79 and 2/27/81 [14]
- Reviewer suggests fans of the Junkie period will enjoy this fairly upbeat performance [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-09-13.168014.mtx.tobin.flac16**: transferred by AUD1 + AUD2 Matrix 3 Source Mix (44/16) by Kevin Tobin; source: AUD1 + AUD2 Matrix 3 Source Mix (44/16) [1]
- **gd1983-09-13.168015.dts.tobin.flac16**: transferred by DTS-Audio-CD 5.1 Mix by Kevin Tobin; source: DTS-Audio-CD 5.1 Mix [3]. Also: DTS surround mix made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in July 2024 [3]
- **gd1983-09-13.151515.fob.unknown.bryant.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Robert Bryant; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Robert Bryant's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; unknown mics > Sony D6 [4]. Also: A 0:15 patch from a Sennheiser 441 source, via Jeff Silberman and Miller, covers the Throwing Stones to Not Fade Away transition [4]
- **gd83-09-13.aud.dodd.12483.sbeok.shnf**: source: ACM> ??> CDR [6]. Also: Audience recording went from cassette to CDR, then was converted to SHN by Ernie Dodd [6]
- **gd1983-09-13.senn441.miller.83117.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Sennheiser 441 -> PCM -> Dat [7]. Also: Taper did a fine job, and Charlie Miller worked on the transfer [23]
